themes.label: Decrees
themes.rationale: The text follows the standard Athenian decree formula, including the archonship, prytany, and the decision of the council and people.

themes.label: Honorific Inscriptions
themes.rationale: The primary purpose of the inscription is to honor Phyleus and his fellow hieropoioi for their virtuous service to the state.
themes.quote: ἐπαινέσαι τὸν ἱεροποιὸν τῆς βουλῆς καὶ τοῦ δήμου... καὶ στεφανῶσαι χρυσῷ στεφάνῳ

themes.label: Accounts and Financial Records
themes.rationale: The decree contains specific financial instructions for the treasurer regarding the funding of the golden crown and the publication of the stele.
themes.quote: τὸ δὲ ἀργύριον τὸ εἰς τὸν στέφανον προδανεῖσαι τὸν ταμίαν τοῦ δήμου

themes.label: Lists of Officials or Citizens
themes.rationale: The text names several officials, specifically the hieropoioi (sacred officials) and the archon, as part of the official record.
themes.quote: ἐπὶ Πυθοδήλου ἄρχοντος... οἱ συνάρχοντες ἱεροποιοὶ λέγουσιν Παυσανίας καὶ Χαρίδημος

themes.label: Stele
themes.rationale: The inscription explicitly orders the text to be recorded on a stone stele.
themes.quote: ἀναγράψαι δὲ τόδε τὸ ψήφισμα τὸν γραμματέα... ἐν στήλῃ λιθίνῃ

themes.label: Marble
themes.rationale: Public decrees in 4th-century Athens, especially those set on the Acropolis, were almost exclusively inscribed on marble, though the text simply specifies 'stone'.
themes.ambiguity_note: The text specifies 'stone' (lithine), but marble is the standard material for such Athenian state documents.

persons.name: Pausanias
persons.role: Father of Phyleus and fellow Hieropoios

rationale: This inscription consists of multiple Athenian decrees from the archonship of Pythodelos (335/4 BC). It honors Phyleus of Oinoe and his colleagues, who served as hieropoioi (officials in charge of sacred rites), for their conduct and virtue. The text includes standard administrative details such as the prytany, the presiding officers (proedroi), and the secretary, as well as specific instructions for the treasurer to fund a golden crown and a stone stele to be erected on the Acropolis.
